name: Soft Center of Plain Hopper (Appa)
preparation_instructions: Prepare fresh plain hopper using rice flour batter.
Tear off the soft, spongy central portion.
Remove crisp, brittle outer edges to prevent throat scratching.
Hand to the child to practice grasping and biting under supervision.
safety_precautions: Adult supervision mandatory; child must never be left unattended.
Ensure soft center is cool before offering.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Soft center of hopper introduced as a chewable finger food at 8 completed calendar months.

name: Soft Egg Hopper (Biththara Appa)
preparation_instructions: Swirl hopper batter in pan, break a fresh whole egg into the center.
Cover and steam-cook thoroughly until the egg yolk and white are completely cooked through.
Tear into manageable soft pieces for the toddler.
safety_precautions: Ensure egg is cooked thoroughly (no raw or runny yolk).
Allergy restriction: Excluded if egg is restricted.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Egg hopper illustrated in the 16 nutritious snacks gallery for children.

name: Ripe Avocado Slices / Soft Mash
household_portion: 2 to 3 soft slices or 2 tablespoons mash
preparation_instructions: Select a naturally ripe, soft avocado.
Wash peel, slice open, remove pit.
Scoop soft green-yellow flesh and cut into thick, easy-to-grip batons.
Offer to baby as self-feeding finger food.
safety_precautions: Ensure avocado is completely ripe and soft.
Supervise self-feeding.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Piece of ripe avocado introduced as finger food at 8 completed calendar months and in snacks gallery.

name: Hard-Boiled Egg Wedge
preparation_instructions: Boil egg until hard (10–12 minutes).
Cool, peel shell, and slice into soft wedges.
Eligible only if child has already tolerated egg yolk.
Hand wedge to baby to hold and nibble.
safety_precautions: Adult supervision required.
Excluded if egg is restricted.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Piece of hard-boiled egg introduced as finger food at 8 completed calendar months.

name: Boiled Sweet Potato Wedge
preparation_instructions: Wash yellow sweet potato, peel skin.
Boil or steam until thoroughly soft and yielding.
Cut into longitudinal finger-sized batons.
Let child hold and bite.
safety_precautions: Must be tender enough to squash easily between fingers to prevent choking hazard.
Supervise during eating.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Boiled sweet potato finger food introduced at 8 completed calendar months.

name: Ripe Banana Slices / Sticks
household_portion: 1/2 small banana in rounds or sticks
preparation_instructions: Peel ripe ambul or kolikuttu banana.
Slice into rounds or split lengthwise into thirds.
Allow baby to pick up with fingers and self-feed.
safety_precautions: Always supervise while eating.
Ensure banana is ripe and soft.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Banana featured in the 16 nutritious snacks gallery.

name: Soft Ripe Papaya Pieces
preparation_instructions: Peel ripe papaya, discard all seeds.
Cut into soft bite-sized cubes.
Encourage the child to pick up and eat.
safety_precautions: Remove all black seeds thoroughly.
Supervise self-feeding.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Papaya pieces featured in the 16 nutritious snacks gallery.

name: Boiled Green Gram with Scraped Coconut
household_portion: 2 to 3 tablespoons cooked green gram with 1 teaspoon scraped coconut
preparation_instructions: Wash green gram, boil until very soft.
Drain excess water.
Toss with freshly scraped clean coconut and a tiny pinch of salt (after 1 year).
Serve warm.
safety_precautions: Ensure grains are boiled very soft to avoid choking.
Excluded if legumes or coconut is restricted.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Boiled green gram with coconut illustrated in the 16 nutritious snacks gallery.

name: Boiled Chickpeas with Scraped Coconut
preparation_instructions: Soak chickpeas overnight.
Boil until soft and tender (easily flattened between fingers).
Toss with fresh scraped coconut.
Serve under supervision.
safety_precautions: Choking prevention: Slightly crush whole chickpeas before feeding toddlers.
Supervise closely.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Boiled chickpeas with coconut featured in the 16 nutritious snacks gallery.

name: Boiled Cowpea with Scraped Coconut
preparation_instructions: Boil cowpea until soft.
Mix with fresh scraped coconut.
Serve as protein-rich traditional afternoon snack.
safety_precautions: Ensure cowpea is completely soft.
Excluded if legumes or coconut is restricted.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Boiled cowpea with coconut featured in the 16 nutritious snacks gallery.

name: Boiled Manioc with Scraped Coconut
household_portion: 2 to 3 soft small pieces of manioc
preparation_instructions: Manioc preparation protocol: Peel deeply, wash thoroughly.
Boil vigorously in plenty of water with the pot lid completely open.
Drain all cooking water thoroughly once soft.
Serve warm, soft pieces with freshly scraped coconut.
safety_precautions: Mandatory safety rule: Always boil manioc with lid open and discard all water.
Never give undercooked manioc.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Boiled manioc with coconut illustrated in the 16 nutritious snacks gallery.

name: Boiled Jak Fruit Pieces (Kos)
preparation_instructions: Boil young jak fruit (kos) until completely soft.
Cut into small tender bite-sized pieces.
Offer as traditional finger food under supervision.
safety_precautions: Ensure pieces are very soft so child can mash with gums.
Supervise closely.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Boiled jak pieces introduced as finger food at 8 completed calendar months.

name: Buffalo Curd with Mashed Papaya
household_portion: 1/2 cup curd with 2 tablespoons mashed papaya
preparation_instructions: Spoon fresh curd into a clean bowl.
Top with naturally sweet ripe mashed papaya.
Do not add sugar or treacle.
safety_precautions: No added sugar.
Excluded if dairy is restricted.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Curd recommended as dairy alternative for non-breastfed children aged 1–5 years.

name: Plain Natural Yoghurt
preparation_instructions: Serve plain, unsweetened fresh yoghurt.
Can mix with mashed fresh banana or ripe mango if sweetness is desired naturally.
safety_precautions: Avoid commercially sweetened or fruit-flavored yoghurts with added refined sugar.
Excluded if dairy is restricted.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: One cup of yoghurt specified in FHB 1–5 years daily requirements for non-breastfed children.

name: Natural Cheese Piece
preparation_instructions: Cut a piece of natural cheese equal to the size of a matchbox.
Offer as finger food snack or grate over warm vegetables.
safety_precautions: Moderate sodium intake; choose mild natural cheese.
Excluded if dairy is restricted.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Matchbox-sized cheese piece specified in FHB 1–5 years table.

name: Finely Crushed Peanut with Mashed Banana
household_portion: 1 teaspoon finely ground peanut powder mixed into 1/2 mashed banana
preparation_instructions: Nut Safety Rule: Roast peanuts, grind or crush with pestle into an ultra-fine powder.
Never give whole or split peanuts to children under 5 years.
Stir 1 teaspoon of fine powder into mashed banana to create a smooth, nutrient-dense paste.
safety_precautions: Severe Choking Hazard: Whole nuts strictly prohibited.
Must be ground fine.
Excluded if peanut restriction is active.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: Nuts must be crushed or mashed finely before feeding to prevent choking.

name: Fresh Scraped Ripe Papaya
household_portion: About 4 teaspoons freshly scraped fruit (FHB verbatim: about 4 teaspoons as tolerated)
preparation_instructions: Select a clean, fully ripe papaya.
Wash outer skin, slice open, and discard black seeds.
Scrape soft pulp with a clean spoon.
Offer immediately as a fresh between-meal snack without added sugar.
safety_precautions: Prepare freshly before serving; do not store leftover fruit.
Never add sugar or honey.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 7 months + 1 week: introduction of 1 to 2 nutritious snacks between meals, such as fresh scraped fruit like ripe papaya (verbatim portion: about 4 teaspoons).

name: Fresh Scraped Ripe Banana
household_portion: About 4 teaspoons freshly scraped fruit (FHB verbatim: about 4 teaspoons as tolerated)
preparation_instructions: Peel a fresh ripe banana.
Scrape thin, soft shavings along the fruit with a clean spoon.
Feed immediately with a spoon between main meals.
safety_precautions: Ensure banana is thoroughly ripe and soft.
Feed with spoon; do not give whole pieces before finger-food readiness.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 7 months + 1 week: fresh scraped fruit like ripe banana offered as early snack between meals (verbatim portion: about 4 teaspoons).

name: Soft Mashed Boiled Sweet Potato
household_portion: Small portion soft mash (derived guidance: 2 to 3 tablespoons according to appetite)
preparation_instructions: Wash yellow sweet potato, peel skin, cut into small pieces.
Boil until soft and tender.
Mash thoroughly with a fork or back of spoon into a soft consistency.
Serve warm between main meals.
safety_precautions: Ensure sweet potato is soft with no hard unmashed chunks.
No added salt or sugar.

source_citation.publication: Right Food at the Right Time, To Make My Baby Healthy and Bright
source_citation.organization: Family Health Bureau, Ministry of Health, Sri Lanka
source_citation.evidence_description: 7 months + 1 week: boiled sweet potato offered as a nutritious snack between meals. Specific tablespoon portion is derived guidance based on infant appetite.
